newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania cabinet to discuss 1997 budget.
newsitem.headline: Romania cabinet to discuss 1997 budget.

text.p: The Romanian government plans to discuss the draft 1997 state budget before the end of this month prior to parliamentary and presidential elections on November 3, a cabinet official said on Tuesday.
"We will come up with a draft budget by November 1," government spokesman Ioan Rosca said by telephone.
Rosca said that any government emerging after the polls could proceed with the existing draft, or draft a new one. A new government would probably be appointed some time in December.

Last week, Romania's National Forecasting Board issued key 1997 indicator forecasts -- 5.5 percent growth in gross domestic product (GDP) and 20 percent year-on-year inflation -- to underpin the draft budget.

Inflation is expected to stand at about 30 percent for 1996 but economists say the 12-month figure could be higher due to energy and fuel price rises in July. GDP growth is envisaged at 4.8 percent this year.
Year-on-year inflation quickened to 44.2 percent in August from 40.3 percent in July.

Romania's state budget posted a 1.9 trillion lei deficit over January-August, up from 1.66 trillion lei in the first seven months. The budget gap is estimated at 4.27 trillion lei for the whole 1996 year. ($=3,262 lei) --Diana Voicu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
